title: ARCHITECTURE.md links to docs/adr/0001-metadata-service-architecture.md, deleted 2026-02-11 — the link 404s
body:
Found while implementing #6634 (the ADR-0079 dangling-pointer fix); out of that PR's scope, filed unassigned.

## The fact

`ARCHITECTURE.md:653` carries a markdown **link**, not a bare mention:

```
- [ADR-0001: Metadata Service Architecture](docs/adr/0001-metadata-service-architecture.md) - Explains why both ObjectQL and MetadataPlugin can provide metadata service and how they work together
```

That file was **deleted on 2026-02-11** in `9da8e3e72` ("feat(docs): add comprehensive analysis of Permission Protocol...") together with `docs/adr/0002-database-driven-metadata-storage.md` and `docs/adr/README.md`. Verified against the full history (the working clone is shallow by default — this needs `git fetch --deepen` before `git log --diff-filter=D -- 'docs/adr/*'` says anything true).

So a reader of ARCHITECTURE.md who follows the repo's most prominent pointer to "why both ObjectQL and MetadataPlugin can provide metadata service" reaches a 404.

## Why it is not fixed in #6634's PR

Different defect, different fix. #6634 is about a number cited with no record; this is a **link to a path that was removed**, and fixing it means deciding what the correct target is (the explanation may have moved into another ADR, or may need re-homing) — a docs judgement, not a mechanical repoint.

The other two `ADR-0001` sites in the tree are fine and should not be touched:

- `docs/adr/0002-environment-database-isolation.md:122` — "already discarded in v3.4's ADR-0001", legitimate history.
- `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/{project-detail,project-workspace}.page.ts` — these cite **ObjectUI** ADR-0001, a different repo's registry.

## Interaction with #6634's gate widening

The PR for #6634 extends `check:adr-anchors` to assert every cited ADR number resolves, and puts `0001` on a shrink-only `UNRESOLVED_ADR_CITATIONS` allowlist (deleted record, cited as history). The entry's comment names this broken link explicitly and says the allowlist does not bless it — the allowlist is per-number and cannot distinguish "history" from "broken link" at that granularity. Fixing this issue does not require removing the allowlist entry (ADR-0002's historical mention keeps it earning its place).

Note `.github/workflows/check-links.yml` (advisory lane, repo-internal links, restored 2026-08-07) would plausibly have caught this — worth checking why it does not, but that file is under active work elsewhere and is not part of this report.
